segments.text: to such a great yogi who has got such a great will, desire, Dresham Shri Ram, next
sutra, this whole perceived objective world is his own self. Dresham means perceived
objective world, already perceived objective world is his own self or you may translate
it in contrary way, Shri Ram Dresham, his own body is just like an object, he perceives his
own body just like an object, he does not perceive his body with oneness, with eye, eye
consciousness, because he has no ego for that body, body of his, so Shri Ram Dresham,
Dresham Shri Ram, in these two ways you must translate this sutra, this whole objective world is his
own self, Shri Ram Dresham, his own body is his object, he perceives his body as an object,
not as in a subjective way as we do, we perceive our body, am I strong? I am very weak,
who is weak? Self is not weak, body, because body is weak, I am weak, we say I am weak, we perceive
as Shri Ram Dresham as one with your own eye consciousness, but he does not, he perceives his body as an
object, outward object, and he perceives the perceived world of objects, objective world as his own
self because he is one with every being, collectively if he perceives this whole universe as one with eye,
that is good, that is the reality of perceiving, but initially he must not perceive, that this body is
only mine, eye, and he inserts eye consciousness in one's own body, I do not insert eye consciousness in
your body, I must concern, I must insert that consciousness in you too, in everybody, then that is a right
way of perceiving, otherwise it is strong to put only portion of the world in eye consciousness and
other remaining world as objective world, to him this is not the thing, he perceives this objective world as
one with his own self or his own body as object, Yatya Dresham, Bhayam, Arb and Taramva, Tatat Sarvam,
Ahamidam, whatever object is existing internally or externally, externally or internally, Bhayam,
Arb and Taram, that whole class of objective world he perceives as one with his own limbs, limbs of
body, body of eye conscious being, because of this thought ahamidam, I am this whole universe,
Sadashivat Mahasamapatiya, so this Mahasamapatiya means great achievement of supreme eye consciousness,
Mahasamapatiya, great achievement of supreme eye consciousness, just like Sadashiva does.
In the same way he feels this whole universe as his own limbs of body, body of eye consciousness,
no faith in her, not in a differentiated way. Now he explains in another way, Shri Ram Dresham,
as I explained you already, Shri Ram Dhe, De, Pran, Srinu, Rupam, Nila, Jyavad, Dresham, Nathu, Pashevat, Dresh,
his own body, not only this body, gross body of reckfulness and body of dreaming state, body of
sound sleep and body of wiredness, wiredness comes at the time of death because that wiredness
is the link from of this birth and another birth. He enters in wiredness for some time and then
entry takes place in another birth birth and that wiredness remains according to our tradition for
ten days after death. He is in wired for ten days, not Shiva tradition. Shiva tradition is there
is no birth at all. The one who has entered in that supreme eye consciousness there is no birth for him,
there is no death for him. This is Vedic tradition. So this Shri Ram also, this body also which is made of
four elementary worlds, Jagrath, Sopun, Sushafthi, and Shun. Nila Devad, Dresham,
he perceives that just like object, objects, Nathu, Pashevat, Dresh, Taya, Bati, not just as
all other ignorant people perceive their body as one with their own self.
Avaam, Dehe, Bahahecha, Sarvatara, Muryurana, Rasavat, Ayubhaktayu, Pratipati, Ravati. Hence,
in his body or in external world, to such a yogi, this perception takes place,
perception of one next takes place, all around. Just he perceives this whole universe
as Muryur under Rasavat. The Rasavat of the egg of peacock in one nest, that Rasavat is the same color,
at white color, that liquid for formation inside egg. And that Rasavat produce so many colors afterwards,
when it comes out from the egg, of that peacock. In the same way, he perceives that this whole universe is
made of that Rasavat of Chidana. There is no difference between one being and another being.
He perceives the whole universe as one, with that Ananda. It is said in Vidyana Bhairava also.
Bhairava, Saita, Vishubhangu, Vinirgata. Just as waves are not separated from water,
Vahineer, Jyola, Banga, just as the flames, various flames are not separated from fire. Just as
Prabhava Ravi, just as rays are not separated from sun. In the same way, all currents and flows of
universe have come out in the manifestation from Me Bhairava. All currents and flows of
universe have come in manifestation from Me, from that eye consciousness. Bhaktaivobobgibhavine
Sada Sarvatr samsita. This is concluded in Spanda, in this Shloka, that subject to energy,
subject to energy is established in object to energy. Object to energy is no other than subject
to energy. This objective world is one with that subject world. So, this is the kingdom of subject
to world, not object to world.
